walkthroughs.body_html:
Geographic Themes: Freshwater / Oceans & Coastal Margins / Extreme Environments / Geophysical Hazards / Leisure, Tourism & Sport / Food & Health / Urban Environments — a core area of Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Geographic Themes: Freshwater / Oceans & Coastal Margins / Extreme Environments / Geophysical Hazards / Leisure, Tourism & Sport / Food & Health / Urban Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Geographic Themes: Freshwater / Oceans & Coastal Margins / Extreme Environments / Geophysical Hazards / Leisure, Tourism & Sport / Food & Health / Urban Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the breadth of an Exclusive Economic Zone under UNCLOS 1982?
options: 12 nautical miles
50 nautical miles
200 nautical miles
350 nautical miles

mcqs.q: What cell weakening threatens the Atlantic conveyor?
options: Walker
AMOC
Hadley
Ferrel

mcqs.q: Why does urbanisation produce a flashier hydrograph?
options: Impermeable surfaces (concrete, tarmac) reduce infiltration, drains speed up runoff to rivers, shortening lag time and increasing peak discharge — raising flood risk downstream.
Urbanisation reduces flood risk because drains take water away safely.
Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
Urbanisation makes hydrographs flatter because cities use a lot of water.

mcqs.q: Why are urbanisation rates currently higher in LICs than HICs?
options: HICs urbanised earlier and are now near saturation (80%+ urban); LICs are still in the rapid urbanisation phase, with high rural-urban migration and urban natural increase.
Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
LICs have higher urbanisation rates because they have more cities than HICs.
Urbanisation makes hydrographs flatter because cities use a lot of water.

mcqs.q: How are fold mountains like the Himalayas formed?
options: Urbanisation only happens in LICs — HICs are deindustrialising.
By the collision of two continental plates (India and Eurasia) where neither can subduct, so the crust crumples and is forced upwards over millions of years.
Fold mountains form when one plate slides under another into the mantle.
Fold mountains form from giant volcanoes erupting upwards.
